contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #357: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point.
Audit the conditional sharp two-center projection estimate pi:sharp-projection in the staged manuscript; upstream estimates remain hypotheses, not certified conclusions.

definitions.R: 16(L+C_sep+2)>1; S=32R; all balls and norms use dyadic rescaled metric and Hausdorff measure
definitions.s: sqrt(E_i(x)+E_i(z)); v=f^z-f^x; U=R_i(y)^(-1/2)(u-u(z))/r_i; L_z w=<grad f^z,grad w>

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 357 (Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point.; papers: Bi-Lipschitz Coordinates at Regular Points of Noncollapsed RCD Spaces; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Assuming the imported geometric normalization, local calculus, Poisson bounds and radial invariance, there exist C and a late-space threshold uniform in centers and dyadic scales with |b|<=C and ||grad(v-b.U)||_L2(B_(2L+4)(y))<=C s.

If Delta f^z=a in [n,n+1], ||grad f^z-grad(d_z^2/2)||_2<=C s, w is bounded Sobolev on B_4R, L_z w=w+ell.U+k+e with ||e||_2<=C s, alpha=||w||_2(B_R), and |ell|+|k|<=C(alpha+s), then ||w||_2(B_2R)<=C(alpha+s), uniformly even when alpha tends to zero.
The affine L2(B_R) projection residual w=v-c0-b.U is bounded and harmonic and satisfies L_z w=w+ell.U+k+e, ||e||_2<=C s and |ell|+|k|<=C(alpha+s), with uniformly bounded c0 and b.

Under the imported uniform Euclidean compactness regime and C_RT, C_EUL, C_RIG, the affine projection residual satisfies alpha<=C s uniformly over all sufficiently late configurations, hence its interior gradient has the same bound.
A C2 function h on a Euclidean ball satisfying X.grad h=h+ell.X+k is affine; in particular a harmonic such h orthogonal on B_R to 1,X_1,...,X_n has zero L2 norm.
